$comment: Plan WS-H H-4: how each ACVP operation's output is compared ACROSS targets (WASM C++/Rust, native Linux x86-64/Arm64, macOS, i.MX95, KV260). One entry per plan operation (src/services/acvp/dispatch.ts). 'byte-equal' = the response field must be identical to the reference (hex compared case-insensitively, as ACVP hex is); 'semantic' = outputs legitimately differ between correct implementations (randomised), so a target passes only through the named semanticCheck, and without a recorded semantic verdict the case is 'not comparable' — never 'pass'. Consumed by src/services/acvp-xplat/compare.ts; an operation with no entry here makes the comparator throw.

ml-kem.decapsulate.rationale: ML-KEM.Decaps (FIPS 203 Alg. 18) is deterministic in (dk, c), including the implicit-rejection path: every conforming implementation returns the identical 32-byte shared secret, so any byte difference is a divergence.

ml-dsa.verify.rationale: ML-DSA.Verify / HashML-DSA.Verify (FIPS 204 Alg. 3/5) returns a deterministic boolean for (pk, M, ctx, sigma[, PH]); the verdict must be identical on every target.

ml-kem.encapsulate.semanticCheck: Decapsulate the target's ciphertext c with the matching dk (reference engine) and require the recovered secret to equal the target's k; byte equality with another target is NOT expected because m is drawn from the token RNG.
ml-kem.encapsulate.rationale: PKCS#11 v3.2 C_EncapsulateKey draws m from the RNG, so two correct targets produce different (c, k).

ml-dsa.sign.hedged.semanticCheck: Verify the target's signature under the prompt's pk (and cross-verify on the reference engine); byte equality is NOT expected because rnd is fresh per signature.
ml-dsa.sign.hedged.rationale: Hedged ML-DSA (FIPS 204 Alg. 2, rnd from the RNG) is randomised; PKCS#11 exposes no rnd-injection seam (plan Q6 / D2-4).

ml-dsa.sign.deterministic.rationale: Deterministic ML-DSA (rnd = 0^32, CKH_DETERMINISTIC_REQUIRED) is a function of (sk, M, ctx); every target must produce the identical signature.
